3. READ (do not run) and assess against our protocol:

   - ANY install/setup/bootstrap scripts (.sh, .ps1, Makefile, Dockerfile, postinstall, conda recipes): read them line-by-line.    - Model-weight / data auto-download: does import or first-run fetch large weights from HuggingFace/arbitrary URLs? Note the source + approx size. The user's box is 16GB RAM + RTX 5060 Ti — flag if it needs big VRAM or multi-GB downloads (compute/footprint risk, even if not malicious).
   - Obfuscated/encoded blobs (base64 exec, pickled payloads, eval of downloaded content), cryptominer patterns, high-compute background loops.
4. VERDICT: one of SAFE-TO-USE / SAFE-SOURCE-ONLY-DO-NOT-RUN / SKETCHY-DELETE, with specific evidence (file + line) for anything flagged. If SKETCHY-DELETE, delete the quarantine clone and say so. If SAFE, note whether it's useful for the user's work (neural-mesh/Hebbian-router R&D, or the SaaS ventures) per our "download if safe + check usefulness" policy, and whether it should go in vetted-libraries.md.
5. WRITE the full write-up to `C:\Users\mariu\experiments\vet-agentic-diffusion.md` (real source link, verdict, what it does, compute profile, flags, fit). Do not add it to vetted-libraries.md yourself — just recommend.

Return a concise verdict + the top findings. Remember: inspection only, never execute, delete if sketchy.
